title: Dark Were the Paths Our Master Trod
description: Dark Were the Paths Our Master Trod in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 128, “Christ The Sufferer”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Dark were the paths our Mas-ter trod, Yet nev-er failed his trust in God; Cru-el and fierce the wrongs he bore, Yet he but felt for man the more.

lines: Dark were the paths our Master trod,
Yet never failed his trust in God;
Cruel and fierce the wrongs he bore,
Yet he but felt for man the more.
Unto the cross in faith he went,
Upon the cross his prayer arose
In pity for his ruthless foes.
O, may we all his kindred be,
Still loving man through every ill,
And trusting in our Father's will!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
